coverage_caveat: First-turn execution and native serialization only; an effect can legitimately fail in a generic fixture. No claim of independent verification or complete Godot event/policy support.

integration.transport: OS.execute_with_pipe; nonblocking JSONL; local child process

presentation.limits: Damage/status subset; no complete renderer or UI integration claim
presentation.source: Showdown native turn projected to existing BattleTimelinePlan

reuse_assessment.native_combat: Strong candidate: damage/type rules, status/stages, move effects, abilities, held items, weather/terrain/hazards, switches/forms and native generation-specific gimmicks.
reuse_assessment.species_types_stats_natures_weights: Reusable data/calculation; actual CreatureFactory DTO imports tested, 1082 base/region rows match base stats/types after explicit aliases. Weights are in catalog entries.
reuse_assessment.items: 530 matching item entries. Held-item battle behavior is reusable. Generic item descriptions are not bag-use implementations.
reuse_assessment.capture_bag_escape: Not supplied as adventure commands. Native normal-turn pass is rejected; reaction/failed capture/bag actions need a deliberate extension. Preserve our existing campaign modules.
reuse_assessment.progression_evolution_learnsets: Species/learnset/evolution data can be reference; simulator does not run campaign XP, levelling, shops, inventory, PC or level-slot randomization.
reuse_assessment.trainer_ai: Native snapshots and batches support planning technically; keep our professional policy/memory and feed sanitized plausible worlds. Never use raw authoritative opponent state for real trainer search.
reuse_assessment.multiplayer: Deterministic choice/request/protocol model can support future authoritative battles. No coliseum/lobby/account/network integration provided by this probe.
reuse_assessment.art_world: Keep our existing Godot maps, art and reviewed move clips. Existing timeline accepts the sampled translated native turn; complete event translation remains work.

required_before_production: Define a versioned opt-in backend facade around choices, requests, native snapshot and persistent creature reconciliation; keep legacy in-flight saves on their backend.
Translate the shared protocol/event classes, explicitly reject or flag unknown effects and keep trusted visual state separate from AI/player views.
Preserve HP/PP/status/items/instance identity and temporary form/Dynamax overlays without corrupting PC/campaign data. Legacy sleep/toxic clocks require explicit conversion tests.
Choose a versioned generation/rules profile: native Gen9 rejects Dynamax, while all 19 generated Max moves pass in native Gen8. Hybrid rules are not silently enabled.
Resolve 60 move-field differences (mostly generated Z variants; six other rows), generic Embody Aspect form mapping and external held items such as Smoke Ball.
Adapt failed capture/bag/escape reactions and maintain finite inventory and randomlock/permanent death rules outside the simulator.
Adapt existing trainer observation/action-space/plausible-world/fork boundaries and benchmark actual search workloads, not just the 64-branch experiment.
Package a portable Node/helper or separately evaluate native PSVM/GDExtension; preserve licenses, child lifecycle, timeouts and offline startup. Current experiment uses local development runtimes.
Use integration tests/invariants and external expectations. Comparing the adopted simulator against itself would not independently certify its rules.

alternatives.assessment: README describes work in progress and Godot example planned. Native option for later packaging; not built/tested here, no ready-made Godot integration assumed.
Retained as references. Their generation limits/licensing/dependency issues make them weaker replacement candidates than this tested simulator route.
